items.title: Unabomber Review
items.excerpt: Unabomber covers the formative years and later arrest of Ted Kaczynski, the titular mail bomber who terrorized the US from the late 1970s until the mid-1990s. Director Janus Metz’s mixed bag of a film aims to understand the origin of a domestic terrorist but it never quite convinces or connects.
items.content_text: Unabomber is now streaming on Netflix. Unabomber covers the formative years and later arrest of Ted Kaczynski, the titular mail bomber who terrorized the US from the late 1970s until the mid-1990s. Director Janus Metz’s mixed bag of a film aims to understand the origin of a domestic terrorist but it never quite convinces or connects. As FBI Agent Joanne Miller, Shailene Woodley — decent in a two-dimensional role almost any actress could have played — leads the surprisingly inert 1990s portions of the film chronicling the manhunt for Kaczynski, then a hermit living in the woods of Montana. This storyline strives for serial killer movie suspense, but it never musters enough thrills to overcome its inherent tropes. It reduces the FBI’s capture to a dull TV cop procedural instead of capturing the magnitude of what was a historic win for law enforcement. What sets Unabomber apart from other projects about this notorious criminal are the portions set at Harvard University during the Cold War. This is where teenage Theodore Kaczynski (Jacob Tremblay), a brilliant mathematics student who yearns to be a philosopher, participates in a harrowing psychological experiment overseen by Professor Henry Murray (Russell Crowe). Murray’s (now clearly unethical) program was meant to stress-test a person’s philosophical arguments, but instead it became an abusive quest to break a person until they changed. (It’s all very Manchurian Candidate .) The movie suggests that Murray ultimately unleashed a monster within Kaczynski who would later target the industrial and academic institutions he blamed for ruining the natural world and robbing humans of liberty. The reality is more complicated . As the prodigy-era Kaczynski, Tremblay, try as he might, struggles to convey the psychological layers of his damaged character. Crowe delivers a fine but rote turn as the doctor who manipulated his student. Murray’s actions certainly make him the heavy of this film, but Crowe plays him with enough haughtiness to prevent the character from being a complete mad scientist cliche. Like Kaczynski, Murray wants the world to know how brilliant he is but he may, in fact, just be a big loser. If you’re on Netflix looking for something worth your while about this subject the better choice to stream would be the 2020 documentary Unabomber: In His Own Words.

items.title: Melissa Barrera Says She Would Reprise Her Scream Role, Reveals Conditions for Her Return
items.excerpt: Actress Melissa Barrera said she is open to returning to Scream, but don't expect to see her reprise her role as Sam Carpenter as long as Spyglass Media has the rights.
items.content_text: Actress Melissa Barrera said she is open to returning to Scream, but don't expect to see her reprise her role as Sam Carpenter as long as Spyglass Media has the rights. The Scream 5 and Scream 6 star opened up about what it would take to bring her back to Wes Craven's legendary slasher franchise during an interview with JustWatch . Barrera explained that she still "loves the franchise," but the people overseeing it are what's keeping her from going another round with Ghostface. "Not with the company that currently holds the rights," she said when asked if she would return if she got a call to reprise her role. "I love the franchise. I had an amazing time making those movies, but a lot of the hate and difficulty that I've faced in the last years is because the leadership of that company made it a point to label me something that I'm not." "And they never apologized, even when I was proven right. Even with an apology, I wouldn't go back to work with them – not that I'm holding my breath. I don't think they have that ability." Barrera starred in two installments for the horror franchise and was set to return for a third run with Jenna Ortega but was fired by Spyglass following a series of pro-Palestine social media posts she published in late 2023 . At the time, Spyglass said it has "zero tolerance for antisemitism or the incitement of hate." "I pray day and night for no more deaths, for no more violence, and for peaceful co-existence," Barrera said in a statement following her firing. "I will continue to speak out for those that need it most and continue to advocate for peace and safety, for human rights and freedom. Silence is not an option for me." The Scream rights holder's move was immediately met with backlash from fans for more reasons than one. Barrera had helped bring the franchise back to theaters after a decade without a new installment, and when she was unceremoniously removed as the lead of Scream 7 , other talent happened to follow suit. Jenna Ortega departed Scream 7 just weeks after it all went down. Director Christopher Landon confirmed his exit just one month after Spyglass fired Barrera. Paramount Pictures and Spyglass went on to release a very different vision for the franchise when Scream 7 premiered earlier this year. Although familiar faces helped it break records at the box office , the latest entry debuted to franchise-low reviews, as shared by Rotten Tomatoes . IGN gave it a 6/10 . Scream 8 is also reportedly in the works. Despite veering off in a completely new direction, Barrera said now that she's open to coming back. For her, it's not just about working under new management but honoring Craven's legacy. "If the franchise were ever to leave those hands and go into hands that would, I think, honor Wes Craven's legacy more… I think, yeah," she continued regarding her interest in a return to the franchise. For now, Barrera remains uninvolved with Scream. Series star Matthew Lillard recently spoke up about his surprise return in Scream 7. During a recent Q&A (via Deadline ), he said he was "embarrassed" to have reprised his role. " I’m just gonna say, what happened to Melissa, the whole world didn’t pipe up," he said. "She was like a year early on what the f**k’s going on, but the whole world should have piped up and said, ‘she’s right,’ and they didn’t. And that’s brutal." For now, Scream 8 has no release date. Although ideas for the next film are something that have been in the works behind the scenes for some time , there's no information about who may show up in it.

items.title: Everything Coming to Disney+ and Hulu in October
items.content_text: In the aftermath of yet another price hike , Disney has revealed next month’s streaming lineup for both Disney+ and Hulu. Why are we talking about both streaming services at the same time? Over the past year, Disney+ and Hulu have been slowly merging their libraries . They also cost about the same as a bundle as they would as individual standalone services, presumably by design. If you’re debating whether to stick with the more expensive subscriptions, here’s a look ahead at what you’ll be getting out of it next month. The topline? We’re looking at a new MCU series, tons of ABC show premieres, and plenty of Halloween specials. Highlights Coming to Disney+ and Hulu Next Month American Horror Story: 13 One of the most anticipated TV streaming premieres is a new season of Ryan Murphy’s fever dream, American Horror Story. Plenty of cast members have returned for the hauntingly significant 13th season, including Sarah Paulson, Evan Peters, Angela Bassett, and Emma Roberts. In other words, expect some wacky crossovers of characters and plotlines from previous seasons. While the first three episodes premiered on FX in late September, they won’t be coming to Hulu until the start of October. Time to get spooky. More TV Highlights: Hulu and Disney+ will also be getting weekly episodes from new seasons of Dancing With the Stars, Abbott Elementary, Scrubs, Grey’s Anatomy, and Always Sunny in Philadelphia. The Hunger Games Movies The Hunger Games movies have moved around streaming services quite a bit over the years. While the full franchise is already available to Netflix subscribers, Hulu will also be getting the full movie marathon this October. Having all of the movies in one place is a great chance to catch up on or rewatch the dystopian saga ahead of a new prequel movie, Sunrise on the Reaping . VisionQuest The biggest Disney+ premiere of the month comes from the MCU side of things. VisionQuest is a new series that follows up 2017’s WandaVision, one of the most acclaimed Marvel projects in the streaming era. While we already know the series will bring back some old-school Marvel characters , cast members have been close-lipped about whether we’ll see the return of the Scarlet Witch herself . All Upcoming Marvel Movies and TV Shows Barbarian Between last year’s Weapons and this year’s Resident Evil , Zach Cregger has been having quite a run. We’d argue that the run started with the director’s debut movie, Barbarian. We called it “one of the wildest horror films in years” in our original 8/10 review , and it’ll be finding a new streaming home on Hulu next month. Halloween Specials Last but not least, it’s definitely worth keeping an eye out for Halloween specials. Family Guy is already confirmed to be dropping its special episode on October 5, while Phineas & Ferb have a Halloween episode slated for October 7. The Simpsons will almost certainly get a new addition to its ongoing Treehouse of Horror Halloween special series on Disney+ some time later in the month. Both services will also be getting plenty of new Halloween sections and streams. items.title: New Werwulf Trailer and Tie-In Video Game Revealed
items.excerpt: Focus Features has released the new official trailer for Robert Eggers’ Werwulf, alongside a surprise video game reveal for the medieval horror film.
items.content_text: Focus Features is releasing all its major marketing and asset reveals for director Robert Eggers’ Werwulf according to the calendar of the full moon . That’s why the new trailer for the medieval horror film dropped today. Werwulf follows a 13th-century farmer (Aaron Taylor-Johnson), who is cursed to live as a werewolf. Lily-Rose Depp plays his wife and the mother of his children, while Willem Dafoe, Ralph Ineson, and Jack Morris play a trio of wolf hunters on a mission to kill the werewolf. You can watch the new trailer below. In addition to the trailer, Focus also announced the Werwulf Alternate Reality Game today. The game is timed to each of the full moons between September through November 2026 and, according to what Focus revealed, “culminates in a mysterious prize for those that complete all three moons each full moon.” Players can visit DevourethAllMankynde.com where they need “to seek out a hidden ‘sign’ on various digital platforms and decipher the sign back into the site in order to fulfill the moon. The catch is, you only get 24 hours each full moon to search for the sign before it disappears so you’ll need to work fast to find it.” The first clue can be found here . For more on Werwulf, discover the latest details Robert Eggers revealed about his “Hell-like” medieval horror film . Werwulf opens in cinemas on December 25.

items.title: John Goodman, Laura Bailey, and Ian Alexander to Star in HBO's The Last of Us Season 3
items.excerpt: Emmy-winning actor John Goodman, prolific voice talent Laura Bailey, and returning star Ian Alexander have been cast in the third (and possibly final) season of HBO’s The Last of Us series.
items.content_text: Emmy-winning actor John Goodman, prolific voice talent Laura Bailey, and returning star Ian Alexander have been cast in the third (and possibly final) season of HBO’s The Last of Us series. As revealed on September 26 — the day the Cordyceps infection ravaged humanity in The Last of Us universe — the show’s third season will feature three big talents, two of whom are making their return to Naughty Dog’s flagship zombie franchise. Perhaps most surprisingly, John Goodman has been slated to play a character named Joey, a figure who wasn’t in the original games. Joey is joined by another character named Paco, who will be played by Ian Alexander; the two are described as a “friendly duo who dub themselves ‘Heroes of the Highway.’” Alexander notably played Lev in The Last of Us Part 2 , a young boy who Abby helps rescue from the Seraphite cult. The Seraphites will play a part in season 3, as Laura Bailey is set to play Elizabeth, one of the cult’s leaders. Bailey is also a returning actor to the franchise, having famously voiced Abby in The Last of Us Part 2 alongside Alexander. With the Seraphites being included in the third season and Alexander playing a new character, it stands to reason that another person will be playing Lev, most likely because Alexander has aged out of the role. These two aren’t the only actors from the original games who have been included in HBO’s screen adaptation; Ashley Johnson and Troy Baker also played characters in The Last of Us Season 1, with Johnson playing Ellie’s mother in a harrowing birth scene and Baker playing James, a member of Baker’s villainous group. Johnson and Baker famously provided the voice and motion performances for Ellie and Joel in both of The Last of Us Games, so it’s not surprising that Bailey and Alexander are also showing up in some way. HBO’s The Last of Us series is expected to end with this forthcoming season, which will air in 2027. In a September interview with Deadline, the Chairman and CEO of HBO and Max Content, Casey Bloys, said he “thinks [showrunner] Craig [Mazin] has planned it as the final season.” Bloys has been hinting at this since January, saying in another Deadline interview that “it certainly seems that way, but on decisions like that, we will defer to the showrunners. So you can ask them.” With the games’ creator, Niel Druckmann, having left the project after Season 2, the future of HBO’s show is looking uncertain — but with talent like Alexander, Bailey, and Goodman on board, there’s bound to be some fantastic performances in store. We just hope they don’t tear our hearts apart like Nick Offerman did in the first season. Image Credits: Henry NICHOLLS / AFP via Getty Images

items.title: Werwulf Director Robert Eggers Reveals New Details About His 'Hell-Like' Medieval Horror Film
items.excerpt: Director Robert Eggers reveals eerie new details about Werwulf, his upcoming medieval horror film starring Aaron Taylor-Johnson, Willem Dafoe and Lily-Rose Depp.
items.content_text: “After Nosferatu, I kind of said, ‘Let me try to write the scariest thing I can write.’ I don't know that I did that, but I definitely wrote the darkest thing,” writer-director Robert Eggers told the press at a promotional event Friday for his upcoming horror film, Werwulf. And based on the roughly 20 minutes of select footage I saw from the film, Werwulf indeed has all the makings of being Eggers’ darkest and scariest movie yet. Werwulf follows a 13th-century farmer (Aaron Taylor-Johnson), simply referred to as Man, who is cursed as a werewolf. Lily-Rose Depp plays his wife and the mother of his children, while Willem Dafoe, Ralph Ineson, and Jack Morris play a trio of wolf hunters on a mission to kill the werewolf. Eggers kicked the event off by screening the opening scene of Werwulf, a dialogue-free nighttime sequence. The howling of wolves can be heard over a black screen. Then the Man’s face is revealed. He is foaming at the mouth and in great pain. The Man sprints naked through the woods and enters an empty home. Inside, he suffers wild convulsions in the moonlight and growls in agony. He writhes on the floor, and eventually ends up in the shadows where his transformation continues unseen. Taylor-Johnson performed all these body-bending movements himself (save for one shot that could not be accomplished practically), and it was truly a wild sight to behold. Eggers stressed, though, “that is not the set piece werewolf transformation.” “I think werewolf movies are a difficult genre. And I think sometimes even if it's a great werewolf movie, it's hard to believe that your dad's turning into a werewolf or your next door neighbor who's a high school basketball player is turning into a werewolf,” Eggers said. But a period werewolf movie “really helps ground you and ground the audience. At least that's the intention.” While I won’t give blow-by-blow details of the other scenes in order to avoid spoilers, the additional footage showed: aspects of the Man’s youth; hints at how and why he ended up cursed; the arrival of three wolf hunters at the Man’s home in the middle of the night to violently enlist his help in hunting down a werewolf; and the Man and the hunters’ journey to find a strange old woman who may know a thing or two about werewolves. "It was designed to be kind of like a silent movie. Eggers did copious amounts of research on England in the 13th century for the screenplay, he co-wrote with his The Northman collaborator, Sjón. The film’s dialogue is in Middle English, although it’s been altered by dialect coach William Conacher to make it more comprehensible for the modern ear. Eggers also worked with two Middle English scholars at Oxford University, Eleanor Baker and Daniel Wakelin , who helped make the dialogue more period accurate. Although the dialogue is in Middle English, Eggers said that Werwulf “was designed to be kind of like a silent movie. You don't need to understand what anyone's saying to understand the movie because you're with everyone on an emotional level, particularly Aaron and his family.” Eggers’ fascination with werewolf lore goes back to this youth. “The historical werewolves that I had read about starting in high school, they were doing things that were so taboo and hard for anyone to wrap their mind around because it was so extreme that the culture that they existed in said, ‘You can't be a human, you must be a werewolf.’ So it was going to be very dark and very primal subject matter,” the filmmaker said. “I wanted to make it in England and because Edward I was trying to protect the wool trade around the time of this movie, he set a campaign to exterminate all the wolves. Actually, Willem's character is based on a real person who did such a good job that in another 200 years there were not wolves in England. So without wolves, you don't have werewolf lore. So if I was going to set it in England, it had to be this early in history around 1300. And that was even more exciting, because the world would be so primitive and so visceral and primal that that would make this all the more dark and brutal.” "’Does this take place in hell? The world of Werwulf is so dark and brutal that Eggers’ said cinematographer Jarin Blaschke texted him after he first read the script and asked, "’Does this take place in hell?’ And it needs to be hell for Aaron. And I think some medievalists would be annoyed that I'm kind of clinging to the stereotype of the Middle Ages being so muddy and dirty and rainy and miserable, but it needs to be so muddy, and rainy, and dirty, and miserable, and shit-covered, and it does need to be hell. But again, I always find that doing the research about the period, you learn stuff that makes it more interesting and more specific. And for this particular movie, more hell-like.” Audiences will discover for themselves just how hell-like Werwulf is when it opens in theaters Christmas Day.
items.title_en: Werwulf Director Robert Eggers Reveals New Details About His 'Hell-Like' Medieval Horror Film

There are several models currently reduced at Amazon UK, ranging from the more affordable Sonicare 2100 Series to the considerably fancier DiamondClean Prestige 9900. items.title: Delta Force Celebrates Its Second Anniversary with New Season Reorientation
items.content_text: Delta Force’s mission has always been to incorporate player feedback to create the best experience possible for its players. As Delta Force players prepare for the free-to-play first-person tactical shooter’s second anniversary, the developers at Team Jade have been hard at work, listening to two years of player feedback as the game has evolved since its initial PC launch, since coming to mobile and Xbox Series X|S. The second-anniversary celebration kicks off September 26th, with daily tasks that offer players the chance to grab up to 3900 limited-time Delta Tickets, and new collectibles like a new legendary appearance for the AUG, called Golden State. But Team Jade also has big plans for the game's future content, which includes anniversary rewards, a suite of new gameplay experiences, and quality-of-life improvements. Delta Force is getting a serious – and seriously major – upgrade. The roadmap is evidence of how Delta Force uses community feedback to expand the range of ways players can play, all while improving the overall experience. Team Jade has listened to players, and has crafted a season that’s focused on reducing friction and giving players more time to do what’s most important: playing the game. Let’s get into everything that’ll be coming to your fingertips in the near future. In early 2027, players will get to explore Siege: Valkyrie, a new Operations map powered by Unreal Engine 5 technology. That’s right, Unreal Engine 5 features are being implemented in Delta Force. Siege: Valkyrie takes players to a city under siege. The grand new map is divided by a giant city wall, which gives players two distinct areas. The inner city is extravagant and wealthy, full of opulent high-rise buildings, but rife with danger. The outer city, conversely, finds people struggling for survival and resources against the backdrop of fallen buildings. Each of the areas has its own rules, risks and rewards. Will you decide to extract safely with what you’ve found, or will you take a risk and move deeper into the city in pursuit of a huge payout? The choice is yours. For the first time in Delta Force A big shakeup: for the first time, players from different difficulty tiers will enter the same match. In Siege: Valkyrie, there’s a new high-stakes Operations experience where nothing is what it seems, and nothing is predictable. Operations isn’t alone in getting a big Unreal Engine 5 upgrade. Warfare will be receiving UE5 features, and The Mog, a map that launched with Season Reorientation, is the first map to support them. And yes, even more Warfare Maps are coming, with the next scheduled to arrive in November, and further maps and gameplay modes are planned throughout 2027. Speaking of new gameplay modes, Detonation, a new bomb-defusal mode, is entering beta on September 27th. That beta will be for PC and mobile players worldwide, with consoles getting access later in the year. Detonation pits two battling teams against one another in a race for control. Those on the attacking team have to break through enemy defences to plant a bomb. Conversely, defenders battle to hold their ground, and prevent the bomb being planted. If the attacking team does manage to plant the bomb, the defenders must sprint to defuse it before it’s too late. Each round of Detonation finds players making unique tactical decisions as teams fight for all-valuable positioning, and seek to exploit an opening that could turn the tides of battle. For those interested in the lore of Delta Force, the first volume of Operator Archives is available today. It’s a story series that will explore backgrounds of your favourite Delta Force Operators. That will launch through the game’s official channels, with Operator Quarters planned for early 2027, which gives players a dedicated space to customise, unwind, and socialise with friends. Two years in, and Delta Force’s competitive scene continues to grow, and the future is bright. RISE Series 1 concluded in August, with regional titles won by Dark Entities (EMEA) and Evil Geniuses (US). WIth that, the expanded RISE Series Season 2 is underway. The Delta Force invitational is also coming to DreamHack Stockholm from November 27-29. The invitational is Delta Force’s first major offline event outside of Asia. Season Reorientation, the first part of Delta Force’s second-anniversary celebrations, is live now. It’s bringing some quality-of-life improvements, all designed to get you playing seamlessly. Team Jade has also reduced the time you can spend preparing for battle, adding the option of one-click loadouts. There’s the new Combat Support Fund, an in-game loan system that helps cover the cost of valuable items, ensuring you can get what you need for your loadout faster and more efficiently. There are also key updates to make it easier for new players to be a part of Delta Force. A revamped G.T.I Field Manual provides all the in-game information you need to play in easily accessible fashion to ensure that jumping into the world of Delta Force is fun and straightforward. It also allows for existing players to introduce friends, highlighting the importance of building community. And those playing for the first time will enjoy a new redesigned tutorial. For experienced players, Operations mode is getting a big shake-up with the map Layali Grove 2.0, which introduces new exploration activities. Expanded river areas give players new locations to explore. It’s not all about shooting, either! With all the new water, fishing provides an opportunity for players to breathe in the new environments. It’s not a mere distraction, however, as fishing comes with its own progression system, as well as map-specific catches, which you can in turn display in your Collection Room aquarium. Though those are some of the more relaxing options to enjoy in Operations mode, Season Reorientation is bringing new additions to the more intense, action-packed side of Operations. Play-as-a-boss is back in Polaris Patrol, where you can become the powerful Security Director Desmoulins, who is backed by the Polaris Squad and linked to the Requin armed vehicle. Listening to player feedback, Team Jade has reworked the encounter, ensuring a more balanced play-as-a-boss experience so every side gets a fair chance and richer rewards. In Delta Force’s Warfare mode, there’s a new map, The Mog, which brings with it a new convoy escort experience. Inspired by Black Hawk Down , The Mog focuses on a defecting Skynet engineer caught between G.T.I. and Haavk. G.T.I is tasked with escorting the convoy through a series of checkpoints, while Haavk is determined to stop it. Black Hawk helicopters can join the fray, too, and players are able to deploy directly onto them to operate weapons, or even take on repair duties to keep them flying. With its ever-expanding eSports scene, Season Reorientation and the two year anniversary, Delta Force is continuing to evolve with its community, implementing player feedback while adding new ways to make the most of the game. Delta Force is free to play and available now on Playstation 5 , Xbox Series X|S , Android , iOS , Google Play , Epic Game Store, and Steam .
items.title_en: Delta Force Celebrates Its Second Anniversary with New Season Reorientation

items.title: Marvel's Wolverine Dev Adds Option to Turn Off Controversial Scent Trails and More in New Update
items.excerpt: Insomniac Games has published a new Marvel's Wolverine update that adds an option to turn off those controversial scent trails for collectibles.
items.content_text: Insomniac Games has published a new Marvel's Wolverine update that adds an option to turn off those controversial scent trails for collectibles. The Sony developer made good on its promise to investigate a proper on/off option when version 1.001.006 launched just hours ago. Its patch notes reveal more targeted changes as the studio works out the remaining kinks that have emerged in the days since Marvel's Wolverine launched for PlayStation 5. There are three new toggle settings that players can now use to customize their gameplay experience: one for Whiskey Bottle scent trails, one for Material Crate Audio Clues, and one for Nightmare Door Roots. Those first two proved to be an especially hot topic online, with players criticizing in-game hints as one of a few examples of a game many feel is too 'hand-holdy.' Adding the option to completely turn these guides off should quiet those concerns, with a toggle for Nightmare Door Roots adding even more freedom for players to tailor their Marvel's Wolverine experience to their liking. The new toggles are pretty straightforward. If players find the wavy visuals to be a bit too distracting, they can simply turn them off. As noted in the in-game settings, using Wolverine's Crate Finder and Whiskey Finder Adaptations will override any flipped toggles. The update also tackles some crashes reported by the community, as well as a few pesky glitches. For example, one of the more common problems fans may have seen in viral clips online was Logan getting his claws stuck when sliding down an early-game tree. Insomniac said that should be fixed now, with an issue tied to misaligned claws in photo mode fixed, too. Another squashed bug outlined in the patch notes involves some strange bathroom signs. Players feared the signs suggested Insomniac had used generative AI in Marvel's Wolverine before the studio stepped in to deny the accusations with an explanation . They won't be an eyesore going forward. Instead of fans spending their time talking about the new Wolverine game's mutant-filled story or its bloody action, the conversation surrounding the launch of the new PS5 exclusive mostly revolved around things like scent trails for collectibles, a motorcycle chase sequence , and 'fart gas.' Although the new update can make it more difficult to search for and find Whiskey Bottles and Material Crates, story-driven scent trails and senses – like the one that allows Logan to track Jean in The One That Got Away mission – will remain regardless of toggled settings. On that front, Insomniac has taken measures to make story scent trails a bit less intrusive. Last week's update reduced trail opacity, effectively nerfing the so-called fart gas without completely removing it from the experience. Marvel's Wolverine launched for PS5 September 15, 2026. In the wake of controversy surrounding certain mechanics and features, Insomniac said it would keep its ear to the ground when it came to community feedback . It's a message studio director of community and marketing James Stevenson repeated following the new update. "As I have said we continue to listen and work with the team to address feedback and requests," he said on X/Twitter . Marvel’s Wolverine is out now exclusively on the PlayStation 5. You can read our review of the game here, or peep our 17 Essential Tips and Tricks to help you get started in Marvel’s Wolverine, plus our recommendations for the 10 Best Adaptations , and a guide on How to Farm XP Quickly . Check out our full Marvel’s Wolverine Walkthrough for a step-by-step guide to every mission, and make sure you don’t miss a thing with our Collectibles guides for Whisky Bottle locations to help boost your Adaptations and Weapons Crate locations that help you unlock all Wolverine Suits and Claws , and our thorough list of all the Easter Eggs and References we've found. Oh, and it's only 20 hours to a Platinum Trophy according to our reviewer, here's a guide to that ! Marvel's Wolverine Update 1.001.006 *NEW* Update 1.001.006 This update includes Senses toggles for Whisky Bottle Scent Trails, Material Crate Audio Clues, and Nightmare Door Roots. It also addresses several community-reported crashes and bugs. Full hotfix notes below: Adds new on/off Senses toggles for*: Whisky Bottle Scent Trails Material Crate Audio Clues Nightmare Door Roots Addresses several crashes identified through crash logs & the community Fixes an issue where players could become stuck while sliding down tree in the "The One That Got Away" mission Addresses issues with misaligned claws in Photo Mode Fixes rare issue where objects may turn white after extended play sessions Fixes overlapping bathroom sign in the casino caused by a UV mapping issue *Story-critical Senses will still appear in the world.

items.title: Chris Hansen Announces His Own Documentary After Watching 'Fever Dream' Primetime and Grades Movie a D
items.excerpt: Chris Hansen says he was more confused than offended by Lance Oppenheim’s Primetime, and is answering this dramatized version of events with his own documentary.
items.content_text: Chris Hansen says he was more confused than offended by Lance Oppenheim’s Primetime, and is answering this dramatized version of events with his own documentary. Chris Hansen has finally seen Primetime , which he watched in a Times Square theater alongside an audience of average moviegoers — and he says he was more baffled by the film than anything else. He’s also got “a number of documentaries” about his life and career in the works, one of which is currently being shopped around to multiple different platforms. Hansen delivered the news during an interview with fellow host and journalist Jesse Watters on his YouTube channel after watching Primetime, where he revealed the documentary’s title: I am Chris Hansen. “It’s a project, a film, in which I cooperated, produced by folks obviously I know and work with, and it was in the works well before we even heard of Primetime,” he said. “It’s pretty good timing to have this thing out there with our agents shopping it on the West Coast to various platforms.” Hansen went on to give his review of the movie, which he graded a D. (Hey, at least it wasn’t an F.) And while Hansen praised Robert Pattinson’s performance, he felt the actor’s portrayal of him deviated significantly from who he was as a person — to the point where it was like watching a totally different person on the screen. And that, for Hansen, makes it so separate from his own identity that it’s hard to be offended by it. “What was in it, in my mind, was something that was so overly-dramatized, so detached from reality — as the director put it, a fever dream — that it almost hit me as something that was so far from reality that it wouldn't even bother me, and I think other filmgoers will experience the same thing. “In a way, it's a hit piece on me and the series, which is weird, because all we do is expose bad human beings who try to hurt children. So in that respect, it's sort of an insult to the thousands of men and women who want, every day, to do the same thing that I try to do in Takedown and did in To Catch a Predator. It's so far over the top that it's hard to come to grips with what they're trying to do here.” Hansen went on to mention a specific scene in the film where Pattinson sits in front of a vanity mirror, shirtless, rehearsing what he plans to say to the supposed predators when he gets them on camera. This, like "almost every one” of the other scenes in Primetime, “didn’t happen,” according to Hansen. Hansen went on to reiterate that he was never approached by A24 about the film. Previously, he claimed that he’d refused to sign a waiver before entering a screening of the movie, alleging that the studio wanted him to “sign away my rights.” Prior to seeing the film, Hansen slammed it as a “very dramatized version” of events and even purchased advertisements for his own true crime network to air before every single screening of Primetime. In contrast to Hansen’s opinion, we at IGN scored the film a glowing nine out of 10 , calling it a “blast from the past with a sickly allure” that’s “as garish as its subject: Chris Hansen’s To Catch a Predator.” Image Credits: Mike Pont/WireImage via Getty Images

items.title: How to Play the Silent Hill Games in Order
items.content_text: Silent Hill has appeared in the restless dreams of horror fans for almost three decades now. The foggy town and its various iterations, plagued by the Otherworld, continue to define the mechanics and ambience of psychological horror to this day. Each Silent Hill game contains a relatively standalone story, tied to whatever character the Otherworld has decided to bring to its doorstep. However, the lore of Silent Hill develops across games through returning characters as well as memos, posters, and other small details. Despite its fill of contradictions, some of which are only natural for games with multiple endings, there’s a larger story lurking in the background of each protagonist’s path to atonement (or madness). If the release of Silent Hill: Townfall has sparked your curiosity about how the timeline all fits together, we’ve got you covered. Note: This is not a timeline of the town of Silent Hill, which is revealed throughout games, comics, books, and other supplementary materials. Instead, it’s focused on which games connect to one another and how, with some discussion of each game’s multiple endings. How Many Silent Hill Games Are There? Approximately 18 Silent Hill games have been released since the franchise debuted in 1999. Four Silent Hill games were originally developed by Team Silent between 1999 and 2004. Subsequent games, including plenty of spinoffs, were developed by a variety of studios across Japan and North America. Konami has also published four Silent Hill games for mobile devices: The Orphan trilogy and Silent Hill: The Escape . These have some murky connections to the rest of the franchise. For simplicity’s sake, we are not including these on the full timeline, but there’s still some lore in those for anyone trying to get the full Silent Hill picture. We also won’t be including the Play Novel , which reimagines the original game, or the interactive streaming series Silent Hill: Ascension . Main Silent Hill Games in Release Order: Just looking for a quick list of the hits? These are what we’d consider the most important Silent Hill games in release order, with the first four games making up the “major canon:” Silent Hill Silent Hill 2 Silent Hill 3 Silent Hill 4: The Room Silent Hill: Origins Silent Hill: Homecoming Silent Hill: Downpour Silent Hill ƒ Silent Hill: Townfall Which Silent Hill Game Should You Start With? Where to start is really a matter of what drew you to the series and whether you’re interested in the original gameplay. If you’re looking for a taste of the series on modern consoles, Bloober Team’s Silent Hill 2 remake is a faithful recreation with some quality of life improvements. If you’re interested in Silent Hill for lore reasons, there’s no harm in starting at the beginning or even with the original Silent Hill 2. Unless you still have a PS1 and can somehow get your hands on an original copy (very cool, if so), your best bet here is looking for emulation guides. Every Silent Hill Game in Timeline Order The first four Silent Hill games are considered the “major canon,” with subsequent spin-offs and standalone games making references to the original story, but also creating some contradictions. Some games are directly connected, some loosely reference one another, and others are pretty much entirely their own thing. Still, we have a rough sense of when these games take place, and it’s up to you how they fit into your understanding of the Otherworld. 1. Silent Hill ƒ Release Date: September 25, 2025 | Read IGN's Full Review The timeline of Silent Hill games actually starts with one of the most recent installments. Silent Hill ƒ takes us to the town of Ebisugaoka in the 1960s, marking the first time the series was set in Japan . While some loose connections to the lore of the American Silent Hill are revealed through memos and documents, Silent Hill f’s characters, locations , and “version” of the Otherworld are entirely distinct. You play as Hinako, a teenaged girl living in fear of her own future and family, with a unique approach to save states and endings enhanced by writing from Ryukishi07 . 2. Silent Hill: Origins Release Date: November 6, 2007 | Read IGN's Full Review Silent Hill Origins is a prequel that, despite releasing later, directly connects to the original Silent Hill and Silent Hill 3 as part of the “Alessa Gillespie” arc. It also marks the start of some inconsistencies and, despite its direct connection to the mainline games, is debated in its place as canon. The story, which by in-game logic takes place around the late 70s, follows the truck driving Travis after a crash brings him to Silent Hill. There, he slowly discovers the cult-driven secrets of the town while reckoning with his own traumatic childhood. It’s specifically the “Good” ending from this game that leads into the original Silent Hill, quite literally paving the way for the character of Cheryl. 3. Silent Hill Release Date: February 23, 1999 | Read IGN's Full Review The original Silent Hill, naturally, stood on its own two feet. It introduced us to the opaque fog that, while serving a practical purpose around real-time generated environments, became the series’ atmospheric staple. In the late 80s (if you go by Silent Hill 3 logic), a mysterious car crash leads Harry Mason to the eponymous town of Silent Hill. There, he searches for his now missing young daughter, Cheryl, while encountering the original strange cast of characters and nightmares of the Otherworld. While the canon on this is a bit iffy, we can now think of it as continuing from the “Good” ending of Silent Hill: Origins. And, of course, paving the way for everything else. Note: Silent Hill: Shattered Memories , released in 2009, is a reimagining of this first game with different narrative beats. It functionally takes place within its own timeline, but we’d recommend having some familiarity with the first game to get the most out of it. 4. Silent Hill 2 Release Date: September 25, 2001 | Read IGN's Full Review Perhaps the best-known game in the series, Silent Hill 2 extends the lore of the town from the first game while introducing new characters and plotlines. And, of course, it gave us the iconic Pyramid Head. James Sunderland heads to Silent Hill after receiving a letter from his deceased wife saying that’s where he can find her. Art director Masahiro Ito has mentioned the game taking place in the late 70s, but documents in later games peg Silent Hill 2 as taking place about a decade after the original. The 90s timeline slot aligns with the dates we see in a number of diaries, and is thus what we’re going with. Unlike some of the other games on this list, Silent Hill 2 does not necessarily have a “canon” ending that directly leads to future events. Note: The 2024 remake from Bloober Team follows the same beats as the original story, though with some changes to possible endings . 5. Silent Hill: The Arcade Release Date: July 25, 2007 Now we’re getting into spin-off territory. Silent Hill: The Arcade is particularly unique, focusing more on action shooter mechanics than the eerie psychological horror elements the rest of the series is known for. Still, it’s Silent Hill, and specifically a spin-off game that takes place around the same time as Silent Hill 2. While it’s generally its own thing, Arcade still offers some interesting insight into earlier Silent Hill history, particularly the sinking of the Little Baroness ship back in 1917. 6. Silent Hill: Townfall Release Date: September 25, 2026 | Read IGN's Full Review Yep, things get weird again. The latest Silent Hill game takes place in 1996 on the fictional island of St. Amelia, which places it firmly in the middle of the original Team Silent games. Protagonist Simon wakes up at the docks of the island with no memory of how he got there. In typical Silent Hill fashion, he quickly encounters some funky characters and his own variation of the Otherworld. These encounters slowly reveal his and the town’s past, and how exactly they’re connected. Like Silent Hill f, Townfall has looser connections to the initial cult elements of the series, instead staying connected through themes of guilt. And, of course, the joke ending . 7. Silent Hill 3 Release Date: August 5, 2003 (NA) | Read IGN's Full Review While Silent Hill 3 doesn’t technically pick up the story until after Townfall, it most directly follows the events of Silent Hill: Origins and the original game, concluding the aforementioned Alessa arc. Its place on the timeline generally lines up with its own release year in the early 2000s. The connection here is pretty blatant. You play as Heather, daughter of Harry Mason. The murder of her father (the OG protagonist) prompts Heather to return to Silent Hill 17 years after the first game to learn the true circumstances and implications of her birth. 8. Silent Hill 4: The Room Release Date: September 7, 2004 (NA) | Read IGN's Full Review The last Silent Hill game originally developed by Team Silent carries on from Silent Hill 3 in the early 2000s. One letter in particular clarifies that it’s been a “few years” since the events of the third game. We’ve since gotten plenty of different iterations of what exactly makes “Silent Hill,” but this was the first game to literally move the game’s location away from the specific town, instead bringing us to Ashfield. There are some character connections to the second and third games, but this one largely stands on its own as you try to help Henry Townsend escape his apartment (and the “Nightmare”). 9. Silent Hill: Homecoming Release Date: September 30, 2008 | Read IGN's Full Review Homecoming was the first "mainline" Silent Hill game released after Konami disbanded Team Silent. It once again leaves out the actual town of Silent Hill, instead following the protagonist, Alex Shepherd, as he returns to his hometown of Shepherd's Glen. Homecoming doesn’t have a particularly concrete place on the timeline, but it generally takes place within a few years of The Room. Travis the truck driver makes an appearance, marking a loose connection to Origins, and the game directly addresses the cultish machinations of “The Order” from the original canon. 10. Silent Hill: Downpour Release Date: March 13, 2012 | Read IGN's Full Review Downpour is pretty standalone in the grand scheme of things. However, it does bring us back to the actual town of Silent Hill through the classic means of a sad man getting into a car (well, prison transport bus) crash. There’s not an obvious in-game year attached to the story of Downpour, but general fan consensus places it around the release date of the game itself. Despite its titular setting, there aren’t too many references to the other Silent Hill games, but a certain Pyramid Head does make an appearance. In the joke ending , at least. 11. Silent Hill: Book of Memories Release Date: October 15, 2012 | Read IGN's Full Review Yep, another funky spin-off. This one is particularly distinct, in large part because it’s the one Silent Hill game where you create your own character . It’s also your birthday! And it's a dungeon crawler! Again, a weird one. In all of its weirdness, though, we do know that Book of Memories takes place very specifically in 2010. Just don’t expect too much insight into the rest of the franchise. 12. Silent Hill: The Short Message Release Date: January 31, 2024 | Read IGN's Full Review The timeline ends with a recent free-to-play spin-off that followed the cancellation of P.T. and is once again generally its own thing. The Short Message takes place in “modern day” Germany, specifically the small town of Kettenstadt. Events like the COVID-19 pandemic appear in-game, bringing us into the 2020s. However, the course of the game’s events are heavily influenced by the town’s history back in the 1930s as well as the childhood of its protagonist, Anita. BONUS: P.T. Sure, it might have been pulled from the PlayStation Store , but P.T. certainly made some waves when it was first released. P.T., which stands for Playable Teaser, was an early demo for the full game of Silent Hills, a collaboration between Konami, Hideo Kojima, and Guillermo del Toro. Unfortunately, the project’s cancellation means we’ll never truly know how it was going to connect to the rest of the series. The Future of Silent Hill Silent Hill fans have had plenty to chew on over the past couple of years with the back-to-back release of Silent Hill ƒ and Silent Hill: Townfall. These were two of the wonkier additions to the full timeline, suggesting Konami’s focus is now on experimenting with what exactly can (and should ) be “Silent Hill”. While Konami has openly discussed annual Silent Hill releases , we have yet to hear any official announcements about future new games in the franchise. We do know that Bloober Team is following up their Silent Hill 2 remake with a remake of the original 1999 game . In the meantime, studios continue to take cracks at trying to make a decent Silent Hill movie.

items.title: EA Sports FC 27 Review
items.excerpt: EA Sports stands on shaky ground with a new open-world hub, but the realistic, intuitive Tactics system shows promise.
items.content_text: I find myself in a weird place with EA Sports FC 27. On one hand, worthwhile strategic elements have finally been added that reflect real-world tactics in a concise, intuitive way. On the other hand, the promised improvements to the behavior and pathing of computer-controlled players on the field still ring hollow, carrying over many of the same issues the series has had for over a decade. Couple this with the dreaded introduction of open-world elements via The Grounds, and the result is yet another year where nearly positive change is balanced out by a negative one.Ever since NBA 2K14 introduced MyPark, which eventually evolved into The Neighborhood in NBA 2K18 and The City in NBA 2K21, I figured it was only a matter of time before EA brought a similar open world full of activities to its other sports franchises. While The Grounds isn't without merit, it often feels like EA is trying to solve a problem that didn't really exist. After hours of exploring The Grounds, it’s clear FC 27 didn’t need to have an open-world environment to deliver a more communal online mode. I don’t need to run through a visually saturated, low-resolution city populated by lifeless NPCs just to find a game mode to start up when simple menus devoted to the same function can do that in a more efficient manner. Sure, it works well as an active lobby for matchmaking and makes it easier to find other players and move between activities, but between the framerate drops and unnatural character animations, nothing is immersiveness enough about this hub to justify its existence. The issues above are only compounded by the myriad of unskippable cutscenes and NBA 2K15-level voice acting that make up The Grounds. The irony is that I was initially excited by the new hub world because it brings back one of my favorite FIFA characters from The Journey story mode: Alex Hunter, who first appeared in FIFA 17 and FIFA 18, once again voiced by Adetomiwa Edun. That enthusiasm disappeared quickly once Hunter began speaking, as his delivery feels noticeably more rigid and detached than it did during his original story. Edun's performance nearly a decade ago was passionate and natural, whereas The Grounds' version of Hunter sounds like he would rather be anywhere else. Things get even more painful when Kylian Mbappe appears shortly afterward, delivering his lines with such a stiff, mechanical cadence that it was clear he read them directly from the script all in one take. I honestly found myself grateful that my created character doesn't speak to avoid adding even more uncomfortable interactions. The frustration is only compounded by the constant connection issues and errors that still plague the multiplayer community. From disconnects to server lag, I got kicked from or had to leave more games than I can count in my first full week with FC 27. At one point, I even had a match where my opponent had a goal kick, but instead of kicking the ball, his keeper started floating up the pitch with it. This didn’t end until the poor player was sent back to his home planet like Poochie in The Simpsons. After a few hilarious, confusing seconds, the netminder was able to take his place back between the posts, but I was given a corner kick as a result. The Grounds often feels like EA is trying to solve a problem that didn't really exist. I also played every new minigame, from Mario Kart-like Balloon Ball to Football Tennis. While I had some fun, it wasn’t enough to buck the notion that these elements belong in FIFA Street more than they do FC 27. Combine that with the fact that progression in The Ground is tied to coins and XP that can also be purchased with real money, and it only compounds my worry that the series keeps moving away from the beautiful game I know and love to further push microtransactions. When it comes to gameplay, FC 27's expanded Tactics system and its effect on gameplay is easily the best addition, wonderfully complementing the playstyles and roles introduced over the past few years by improving strategy, movement, passing, and crossing in numerous ways. Now more than ever, you have more control over how teams behave in different phases of play, going beyond basic formations and instructions by explaining the purpose, strengths, and weaknesses of different tactical approaches. This becomes particularly useful when building around individual player attributes. As a Manchester United fan, I found that a deeper defensive approach worked especially well for Noussair Mazraoui, whose patient style lets him maintain his position and disrupt attacks without constantly stepping out of shape, while a short-passing buildup gives him chances to use his technical ability without abandoning that defensive structure. What we said about EA Sports FC 26 "Ultimate Team players have had it bad enough for years, but now, not even the Career Mode players are safe from the Season Pass woes. If you can get past the microtransaction madness, there is a noticeably better soccer game here, and that is worth celebrating – but FC 26 is also EA at its most money-hungry yet, and it’s hard not to worry about where things will go from here." - Ricky Frech, September 26, 2025 Score: 7 Read the full EA Sports FC 26 review . That flexibility became even more apparent when I switched formations on the fly mid-match while playing against Crystal Palace – I found that they were leaving space along the wings, so I moved into a 4-2-2-2, letting Bruno Fernandes operate between the lines and thread passes to a striker such as Benjamin Sesko, creating opportunities for quick combinations and finishes through the middle. Alternatively, when I faced Manchester City, they controlled the wings more successfully. To counter this, I switched to a 4-2-3-1 wide formation, moving Fernandes more centrally so he dictated play and combined with holding midfielders such as Kobbie Mainoo through quick one-two passes. Separating tactical instructions for possession and defensive phases adds another useful layer, while Player Roles give individual players more specific responsibilities within a formation. Instead of simply placing someone in a position and expecting them to behave a certain way, I could build their role around the specific contribution I wanted from them. For example, if I move into a 4-2-3-1 wide and place Benjamin Šeško on the right side, I can adjust his role depending on the circumstances. As an inside forward, he can cut inward to create shooting opportunities or provide another passing option for Fernandes, while a wider role allows him to stretch the defense and open space through the middle.That same flexibility can be useful defensively, particularly when protecting a lead. If an opponent repeatedly targets his side of the pitch, giving Šeško more defensive responsibility lets him drop back and support the right back, providing another way to protect that flank without abandoning the attacking structure. How FC 27 expands the Tactics system is easily the best addition. What makes the system particularly valuable is that it teaches the strategy behind soccer formations without overwhelming players with unnecessary information. FC 27 does a good job explaining why different shapes work, which players suit them, and how to adjust them against different opponents, making the tactical aspect of the sport approachable while still leaving experienced players plenty of room to experiment. This is emphasized even more with revamped passing, which now focuses more on manual controls for grounded and lobbed passing, giving more control over where to place the ball and take advantage of the new curved runs. These movements mirror the real-life game smoothly, as the dynamic movement lets a player burst forward into a curved supporting run around defenders rather than a rigid straight line. While great in theory, these movements can sometimes feel like they work against FC 27’s own computer-controlled behavior. Pathing and defensive logic can still break down on higher difficulties, allowing a carefully constructed gameplan to be undermined by a CPU defender refusing to challenge for a 50/50 ball or making an inexplicable movement. Passing will still occasionally produce similarly frustrating results when a ball aimed toward an open teammate on the right is instead sent toward a covered player in the middle. To confirm it wasn’t just my mind playing tricks on me, I loaded the skill trainer and was about to see firsthand where I was aiming, thanks to the visual aids it provides. It was beyond frustrating to see how many times I’d set up to pass the ball wide right, left, or center to open space, only for the directional bar on the Skill Trainer to snap back toward the nearest defender in the complete opposite direction of where the reticle should be aiming. Revamped defense had similar linger issues, as defensive backs were still getting fooled or pulled off their spot by opposing runners on counterattacks, resulting in far too many uneven counterattack goals. The series is over 30 annual entries deep at this point, yet it still can’t get vital features like passing down pat. That said, I was impressed with the improvements to crossing and corner kicks. Both systems produce more convincing positioning battles and give the player greater control inside the box. I scored several successful headers with Harry Maguire from corners during my time with the game, which stood out because I could count on one hand the number of corner routines and headed goals I had scored in previous EA Sports FC entries. The series is over 30 entries deep, yet it still can’t get stuff like passing down pat. Ultimate Team makes player upgrades much more flexible in FC 27, adding an option to choose between different paths at key stages instead of being locked into a predictable progression. I preferred being able to tailor a player’s PlayStyles and stats to better suit my preferred style of play, and the move toward smaller promo campaigns and a three-PlayStyle+ limit also helps keep special cards from becoming outdated too quickly. While the overall Ultimate Team gameplay and economy balance isn’t drastically different, there are some noticeable issues that clash with some of the revamped systems, specifically for manual goalkeeping and defending. Manual goalkeeper movement is less responsive than in previous testing builds, especially when reacting to crosses and corners, making a hard position even less attractive to want to play. The move to manual skill from automated defending is great in theory, but defenders are easily exploited by pace-heavy attackers if a single player switch is mistimed. I like that matches yield more coins and higher baseline Season Points (SP), but the value improvement is offset by adjustments to base discard values for lower- and mid-tier gold, silver, and bronze cards that make them less valuable and eliminate helpful trading metas like the Bronze Pack Method. Career Mode has also received several meaningful upgrades, especially in the transfer market. I felt much more involved, as the process now features staged negotiations, installments, performance bonuses, bidding wars, and rival clubs attempting to hijack deals. My attempt to sign Manu Koné for Manchester United highlighted this perfectly, as he ultimately chose Manchester City despite me agreeing to both the fee and contract. Player development is also more dynamic in FC 27, with form, fitness, and morale affecting ratings throughout the season, while rivalries, origin stories, starting scenarios, and icon players like Gareth Bale add more variety to Player Career. Unexpected events add further depth through financial penalties, dressing-room conflicts, disciplinary issues, and training-ground incidents, while press conferences now carry greater consequences for morale and squad relationships. I also appreciated that CPU-controlled clubs finally manage finances and recruitment around their tactical needs, making Career Mode substantially deeper overall. Despite these additions, menus are still slow, animations are recycled each season, and a lot of progression is still tied to the dreadful investment system introduced in EA Sports FC 24.
items.title_en: EA Sports FC 27 Review

items.title: Infinity Festival Returns to Los Angeles in November With a Focus on AI
items.excerpt: Infinity Festival returns to the Audrey Irmas Pavilion in Los Angeles this November for its 9th edition, featuring panels and programming focused on how AI is reshaping the entertainment industry.
items.content_text: Infinity Festival, an annual event celebrating the convergence of entertainment, technology, and creativity, is returning to Los Angeles this November for its 9th edition. From November 12-15, the festival will be taking over the Audrey Irmas Pavilion for “four days of ideas, experiences, screenings, demonstrations, and conversations about what comes next.” In previous years, the festival has hosted guests like Avengers directors the Russo Brothers, Brie Larson, Jon Favreau, Project Hail Mary directors Phil Lord and Chris Miller, Jeff Bridges, and many more. This year, the festival promises to dive deep into AI, with panels focusing on its “growing role across the creative industries.” Instead of a standalone track, AI will be present through a broader program “spanning animation, gaming, sports tech, filmmaking, music, virtual production, and live entertainment.” At the event, AI-focused programming will “explore the evolving tools and workflows behind animation and filmmaking, the growing crossover between gaming and entertainment, new technologies reshaping live sports and fan experiences, as well as advances in immersive production and live event design.” Additionally, longtime partners like NVIDIA and HP will participate in the festival’s 2026 programming slate, which will feature “panels, keynotes, screenings, demonstrations, and exhibitions, with speakers and programming to be announced in the coming weeks.” “The changes happening across entertainment and technology aren’t taking place in separate lanes anymore, and Infinity Festival is built for that reality,” said Mark Lieber, Founder and CEO of Infinity Festival. “We’re thrilled to have NVIDIA, HP, and Intel return as presenting sponsors as we bring together the creative and technology communities shaping where these industries go next.” For more information about Infinity Festival, check out www.infinityfestival.com .

items.title: Viral Resident Evil Stunt Footage Shows the Wild Way the 'Katamari Monster' Came to Life in Zach Cregger's Movie
items.excerpt: With Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil movie now in theaters, staff who worked on the film are sharing behind-the-scenes footage of how it all came together, including a jaw-dropping look at the stunt team behind one of its monsters.
items.content_text: With Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil movie now in theaters, staff who worked on the film are sharing behind-the-scenes footage of how it all came together, including a jaw-dropping look at the stunt team behind one of its monsters. Warning: Spoilers for Resident Evil ahead! Resident Evil is known for its wide variety of zombies, but some of the mutations we saw in Cregger’s version of events were brand-new and extremely gnarly. The main stalker monster of the film has been a hot topic of discussion within the games’ fanbase, with many affectionately dubbing it the ‘Katamari Monster.’ If you’ve seen the film and played the Katamari games, you’ll immediately understand why it’s been given this humorous moniker; its specific mutation includes some tentacle-like creatures that reach for other infected bodies and combine them into a mass of arms and legs that rolls around town, much like a Katamari. Most viewers, myself included, figured this monster was a pure work of CGI. But astonishingly, this isn’t the case, as one of the stunt performers tasked with creating its movements proved in a now-viral Instagram post. Jakub Hudlicky, a performer with Movement Production in the Czech Republic, published a series of videos showing himself and several other stuntpeople all strapped together with vests. Working together, the team made their way from one side of a soundstage to another, just like how the Katamari monster moved in Cregger’s film. While the final product was, of course, modeled and put together using computer graphics, its movement was taken from these hard-working stunt performers, with Hudlicky explaining in a comment that the actual footage of them was “not in the final movie, but the movement kinda mimics how the CGI creature moves." Hudlicky said the videos were filmed in July 2025, when he and the stunt team gathered together to figure out how the creature would actually locomote to chase Bryan around Raccoon City. Thanks to their performance, the Katamari monster rolls around like a group of actual human beings using its arms and legs, providing essential information to the CGI artists and animators responsible for creating it in the movie. This is the latest insight from Cregger’s Resident Evil to go viral after the director admitted that its ending wasn’t actually the original conclusion he’d written for the film; instead, he described its final sequence as a “contingency plan” that he’d filmed to “keep the stakes all the way until the end.” “It's like, ‘save him, save him.’ Whereas before it was just like ‘kill them all,’” he explained. Resident Evil has been a major success, garnering mostly positive reviews and becoming the most successful film adaptation of Capcom’s flagship horror game franchise ever. IGN’s Tom Jorgensen scored the flick an eight out of 10 , praising it for being “a simple and exciting survival horror story that benefits greatly from Zach Cregger’s sensibilities.

items.title: The Next Fourth Wing Book Releases Next Week — Here's Where to Buy
items.content_text: Rebecca Yarros' Empyrean Series is getting a new addition next week. Threshing Day is set to arrive on September 29. Yarros announced the new title earlier this year and preorders for the book have been dominating Amazon's best-seller charts since then. Unlike the first three novels in the series, Threshing Day is a collection of short stories detailing the day various characters bonded with their dragons. If you're hoping to pick up a copy as soon as possible, here's the rundown of where to buy and which formats are available. Where to Buy Hardcovers Get it at Target - Sold Out There is only one hardcover version of the book releasing on September 29 and it's part of the Wing and Claw collection. That just means it features the stencilled edges other new releases have all gotten. If you're hoping to pick up a hardcover copy for the lowest possible price, Amazon is the way to go. As the biggest online bookstore in the world, they almost always offer the best deal . Target had also matched that lower price, but preorders have already sold out there ahead of release. The only potential issue with preordering from Amazon is that you won't actually get the book until October. So if you want your copy before then, your best bet is to order a full-price version at Barnes & Noble for in-store pickup. If you'd prefer a normal hardcover edition of the book, you'll have to wait a bit longer. Barnes & Noble and Target are the only stores currently offering preorders for this version and it isn't getting released until October 13. Threshing Day on Audible If you prefer to listen to your favorite romantasy series in audiobook form, the good news is the audio version of the book is releasing at the same time as everything else. The overall best deal on the audiobook is at Amazon where you can preorder it for $14.39. You can also get it for free when you sign up for a free trial of an Audible subscription . There are actually two different audiobooks releasing for this book at different times, the first being of the standard narration variety. If you prefer full-cast audiobooks instead, you can wait for the GraphicAudio version arriving on October 13. Both are eligible for Audible credits or a free trial of the service. The full cast list has not yet been announced, but we already have an idea of what to expect based on previous GraphicAudio releases of Fourth Wing. In addition to multiple voice actors, the audio experience will include music and sound effects. Threshing Day on Kindle For those who prefer to read via their Kindle devices , Threshing Day is also releasing an eBook version on September 29. Other than the audiobook version, this is the quickest way to get access to the book as soon as it releases. You can preorder the book directly from the Kindle Store for $11.99 ahead of its release. Will It Be Free With Kindle Unlimited? Although both Fourth Wing and Iron Flame are available to read via a Kindle Unlimited subscription , that has never been the case for new releases in the series. It is highly unlikely that Threshing Day will be included with the subscription anytime soon.
items.title_en: The Next Fourth Wing Book Releases Next Week — Here's Where to Buy

items.title: Save 40% Off the Sony WH-1000XX "The Collexion" Stainless Steel Noise Canceling Wireless Headphones
items.content_text: Sony's WH-1000 lineup is well-regarded as one of the best wireless noise canceling headphones you can get, with the current generation model being the WH-1000XM6. Perhaps lesser known is that Sony released an even higher end headphone in the lineup earlier this year dubbed the WH-1000XX "The Collexion" . It normally retails for a lofty price of $649, but Secondipity (via eBay) is offering a certified refurbished pair with 2 year Allstate warranty for just $389 with free shipping, or nearly 40% off. According to the reviews from people who have ordered from Secondipity, which is a huge Sony liquidator, the certified refurb headphones are pretty much indistinguishable from brand new. Over 40% Off the Sony WH-1000XX Noise Canceling Headphones Certified refurbished with 2 year warranty The Sony WH-1000XX improves upon the WH-1000XM6 in several ways. The most obvious upgrade is the design and build quality. The 1000XX features a sturdy metal frame that's almost entirely wrapped in hand-brushed stainless steel and vegan leather. Even the buttons are made out of metal. There's very little plastic, especially compared to the 1000XM6. Comfort has been improved here too, with a wider padded headband for more even weight distribution on the head and oversized earcups that are designed to sit around your ears rather than on them.
